title: Dedicated reservation governance and capacity planning checklist
creator: Amira Patel
description: Create a single, operationally-ready governance checklist and lightweight template for intake, approval, and capacity planning of dedicated capacity reservations. This ticket synthesizes PM and infra requirements so that sales, solutions, and SREs can execute reservation requests with clear SLAs, quantitative capacity estimates, and approval rules. The output will be a signable checklist + a prefilled request template that feeds downstream provisioning and forecasting workflows.
acceptance_criteria: A concise reservation request template exists with the minimal fields required to produce a capacity estimate (QPS, model, avg seq len, peak concurrency window, desired SLOs)
Approval matrix defined: automated approvals for low-risk requests, manual multi-stakeholder approvals for high-cost or security-sensitive reservations
Capacity estimation method documented (formula and assumptions) and validated with infra: converts requested throughput into GPU-hour commit and buffer percentage
Runbook links and post-provision checklist are linked (oncall routing, cost reporting, rollback triggers)
Stakeholders sign off: PM, Infra (serving/runtime), Finance, Sales (if customer-facing), and Security where applicable
request_form_template:
Fields (single-line values)
- Customer / Internal team name
- Contact (email)
- Business justification (short)
- Model name and version (e.g., gptx-3.8-q4f16)
- Expected avg outbound tokens / request
- Expected peak requests per second (QPS)
- Peak concurrency (simultaneous requests) and window (minutes)
- Required latency SLO (p95 latency target)
- Desired throughput guarantee (min sustained QPS)
- Start date and term (e.g., 2025-04-01 for 3 months)
- Data residency / compliance constraints (VPC, on-prem)
- Budget constraints / cost center
- Business criticality (none | low | medium | high)
- Requested autoscaling policy preference (aggressive | balanced | conservative)
- Notes / reference links (PRD, contract, trial dashboard)
approval_matrix:
Rules and signoffs: 
- Auto-approve: internal teams with non-customer impact, <= 2 GPU-hours/day estimated, no special compliance flags. Requires PM owner only.
- Requires Infra + PM review: estimated GPU-hours/day between 2 and 20 OR sustained min QPS > 20. Review window target: 48 hours.
- Requires Infra + PM + Finance approval: estimated GPU-hours/day > 20 OR cost > $5k/month. Finance SLA: 72 hours.
- Requires Security review: if data residency == VPC/on-prem OR customer requests dedicated on-prem hardware. Security SLA: 5 business days.
- Emergency/fast-path: Sales can request expedited review for P0 customers; requires explicit e-sign by VP Sales and Infra lead, with post-provision retrospective within 3 days.
capacity_model:
Estimation method (simplified):
Inputs: peak QPS, avg tokens per request, avg tokens/sec generation rate, avg sequence length, model perf profile (tokens/sec per GPU), concurrency factor.
Step 1: tokens_per_second = peak_QPS * avg_tokens_per_request / average_generation_seconds
Step 2: required_token_throughput = tokens_per_second * target_availability_factor (default 1.15 buffer)
Step 3: GPU_equivalent = required_token_throughput / model_tokens_per_second_per_gpu
Step 4: GPU_hours_per_day = GPU_equivalent * 24 * utilization_factor (default 0.6 for burst/cost mix)
Add: safety buffer = max(10% of GPU_hours, 1 GPU-hour)
Notes: Provide worked example inside Confluence link. Model perf profile table must be pulled from runtime-1.18 benchmarks. This model yields conservative commitments; engineering may recommend quantized variants to reduce commitments.
autoscaling_policy_examples: Conservative: min_capacity = committed GPUs, scale_up_threshold = 85% GPU_util, scale_down_threshold = 30%, scale_step = +1 GPU, cooldown = 5m. Use when customer requires hard throughput guarantees.

Balanced: min_capacity = committed GPUs * 0.8, scale_up_threshold = 90%, scale_down_threshold = 25%, scale_step = +2 GPUs, cooldown = 3m, prefetched KV cache enabled. Use for most production workloads.

Aggressive (cost-optimized): min_capacity = committed GPUs * 0.6, scale_up_threshold = 95%, scale_down_threshold = 20%, scale_step = +3 GPUs, cooldown = 2m, TTL-based cache eviction. Best for non-critical workloads with bursty traffic.
